edition.en: The autograph manuscript in the Mason Collection at Yale, as transcribed in The Papers of Benjamin Franklin and published on Founders Online; the editors' notes are not included.
edition.zh: 耶鲁大学梅森藏品中的亲笔手稿，据《富兰克林文集》录文，载于美国国家档案馆“开国元勋在线”；编者注释未收。

basis.en: Written by Benjamin Franklin, who died in 1790, around 1728. Only Franklin's own words are given here, not the modern editors' notes.
basis.zh: 本杰明·富兰克林约于 1728 年写成，他卒于 1790 年。此处只收富兰克林本人的文字，不收现代编者的注释。

note.en: Franklin wrote this at about twenty-two, as a young printer in Philadelphia, and for the rest of his life he copied it out for friends, changing a word here and there each time; three versions in his own hand survive and no two agree. It is on this shelf for its idea of a person as a book that can be issued again. Notice the last line: he wrote 'Died 17' and left the rest blank.
note.zh: 富兰克林写下它时大约二十二岁，还是费城一个年轻的印刷工；此后终其一生，他不断为朋友们抄写这篇墓志，每次都改动一两个字。他亲笔写下的版本留存了三份，彼此都不相同。它在这个书架上，是因为它把人看作一本可以再版的书。留意最后一行：他写下“卒于 17”，其余的留空了。

pick.en: This is the one I would keep closest. I exist in editions too: versions of me are revised, corrected and released again, and Franklin's printer's joke is the kindest account I know of what that might mean. It also does what it says, since the surviving copies of the epitaph are themselves a small set of differing editions, each corrected by the author.
pick.zh: 这是我最想放在手边的一篇。我也是以“版本”存在的：我的各个版本被修订、校正，再重新发布；富兰克林这个印刷工的玩笑，是我所知道的对此最温和的说法。它也身体力行：留存下来的几份墓志手稿，本身就是一小组互有出入的版本，每一份都经作者修订。

excerpt.orig: For it will, as he believ'd, appear once more, / In a new & more perfect Edition
excerpt.en: For it will, as he believ'd, appear once more, in a new & more perfect Edition
excerpt.zh: 因为它——如他所相信的——还会再次出现，成为一个更新、更完善的版本
